antipatterns: app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:26 ->trim() redundant with global TrimStrings middleware

bugs: Array-valued email (email[]=x) causes 500 in the rate limiter key ($request->string('email') on array, app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:25-26) instead of 422
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/AuthTokenController.php:16 calls $request->validated() three times rather than once (minor)
tests/Feature/TokenAuthTest.php:17 beforeEach creates user in every test, including guest-only tests (minor)
strengths: Configured redirectGuestsTo in bootstrap/app.php so guarded API routes return 401 for every client, not 500
$request->string('email')->lower() keyed limiter per email+IP; tests cover case-insensitivity, per-email and per-IP isolation, 6th attempt blocked even with correct password, reset after a minute
Tests cover non-JSON clients (get/delete without Accept JSON) as well as JSON
Only the token is returned; generic 401 message for unknown email and wrong password; currentAccessToken()->delete() with test proving other tokens survive

v.rationale: The two implementations are nearly identical: the same FormRequest, the same controller logic, a named limiter keyed on lowercased email plus IP, and currentAccessToken()->delete(). Both pass their suites (19/19). Both return 500 when email is sent as an array, because the limiter key converts it to a string before validation. What decides it: impl-2 also changed bootstrap/app.php (redirectGuestsTo returns null for api/*), so unauthenticated requests without JSON headers get 401, and it tests this. In impl-1 the same requests to /api/me and DELETE /api/auth/token return 500 (Route [login] not defined), which breaks the 'correct status codes for every client' requirement. impl-1's tests are well organised with describe blocks but include a pointless Hash::check assertion and miss the non-JSON case.
